title: Delhi High Court Orders Takedown of AI-Generated Content Targeting Bollywood Actor Tabu
excerpt: The court examined over 100 URLs across Meta, Google and Reddit platforms as the actor sought protection of her personality rights against deepfakes and digital impersonation.
body:
• Delhi High Court is considering framing a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for personality rights cases involving online misuse
  • Meta agreed to remove 34 Facebook URLs, 71 Instagram URLs and one Threads link identified as infringing
  • Justice Jyoti Singh reserved order on interim relief and listed the matter for further hearing on December 7
  • Tabu joins a growing list of Indian celebrities seeking legal protection against AI-generated content and digital impersonation

Bollywood actor Tabassum Jamal Hashmi, known professionally as Tabu, has moved the Delhi High Court seeking protection of her personality and publicity rights against the alleged unauthorised use of her identity through artificial intelligence-generated content, deepfakes, fake endorsements and digital impersonation.

The case, heard by Justice Jyoti Singh, has prompted the court to consider broader systemic reforms. During proceedings, Justice Singh indicated the court may frame a Standard Operating Procedure to deal with the growing number of personality rights disputes involving online platforms.

"The problem does not lie in policy. The problem lies in how to have a mechanism where it can be nipped in the bud so that it does not go online. It is a larger concern."

— Justice Jyoti Singh, Delhi High Court

Platform Responses and URL Takedowns

Senior Advocate Swathi Sukumar, representing Tabu, presented the court with a detailed list of allegedly infringing URLs organised by platform. The responses from major tech companies varied significantly.

Advocate Varun Pathak, appearing for Meta, told the court that all identified links hosted by the company could be removed. The list comprised 34 Facebook URLs, 71 Instagram URLs and one Threads link. Google's counsel similarly indicated that certain flagged URLs would be taken down.

GoDaddy's representative argued that the dispute also involved domain names, suggesting that suspending the domains would automatically disable all associated URLs. The strongest opposition came from Reddit, whose counsel contended that several of the challenged clips were legitimate excerpts from Tabu's own films — including scenes from the series A Suitable Boy — and did not constitute personality rights violations.

"How is that a violation of personality rights?" Reddit's counsel submitted, arguing that genuine movie clips could not automatically be treated as infringing simply because they were uploaded on the platform.

A Growing Legal Trend

Tabu's petition comes amid a significant rise in personality rights cases before Indian courts. The Delhi High Court alone has recently heard similar pleas from Gautam Gambhir, Sunil Gavaskar, Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, Arjun Kapoor, Allu Arjun, Nagarjuna, Varun Dhawan, Kajol, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, Naga Chaitanya and several others.

In a recent related case, the same court granted interim protection to actor and BJP MP Ravi Kishan against AI-generated videos mocking his speech, fabricated political statements and obscene content using his name. Justice Singh held in that case that "personality rights are now judicially recognised" and that unauthorised use of a celebrity's identity causes "commercial detriment" and affects their "rights to privacy/personality and live with dignity."

Broader Implications for Women in Entertainment

Sukumar highlighted that women celebrities are particularly vulnerable to online abuse and the misuse of their identities. She argued that search results pairing Tabu's name with pornographic terms were being commercially exploited by online platforms.

"For women celebrities, there are issues on the internet. Women and children are very vulnerable online," Sukumar submitted to the court.

Justice Singh observed that similar concerns had surfaced in several personality rights matters previously heard by the court, noting that while platforms may have content moderation policies, the real challenge lies in creating an effective system capable of preventing objectionable material from proliferating at the earliest stage.

What Comes Next

The court has reserved its order on Tabu's application for interim relief. The matter is listed for further hearing on December 7, by which time the court expects a corrected plaint and reconciled URL compilations from all parties. The potential framing of an SOP could set a precedent for how Indian courts handle the intersection of AI technology, digital platforms and individual personality rights going forward.
nri_angle: The case highlights growing concerns about AI-driven exploitation of Indian celebrities, relevant to diaspora audiences who follow Bollywood and Indian legal developments.
